summary: Sinologist and historian of Buddhism Édouard Chavannes studied at ENS, Collège de France, and INALCO under Marie-Jean-Léon d'Hervey de Saint Denys and Maurice Jametel. He held a professorship at Collège de France (1893–1918) and served at EFEO (~1898–1900).

Édouard Huber, a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, studied at Sorbonne, University of Paris, École des langues orientales, and Collège de France, including under Sylvain Lévi. He served as Professeur p. i. de chinois at EFEO (1901–1905).

Linguist, Iranian, and Indology scholar Émile Benveniste studied at EPHE and Paris under Antoine Meillet and Joseph Vendryes. He held posts as directeur d’études at EPHE (1927–1969) and Chair of Comparative Grammar at Collège de France (1937–1969).
Philosopher Émile Chartier studied at Lycée Pierre-Corneille (~1881–1886) and École Normale Supérieure (~1889–1892). He later taught scholar Paul Mus.
Linguist and historian Émile Chatelain studied at École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1872–1876). He subsequently held posts at École française de Rome (1876–1877) and EPHE (~1881–1926).

Scholar of religion Émile Durkheim studied at ENS and Leipzig under Wilhelm Wundt. He held academic posts at the University of Bordeaux (1887–1902), École Pratique des Hautes Études (1905), and Sorbonne University (~1902–1917), and founded L'Année Sociologique (1898).

Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar Émile Senart studied at Munich and Göttingen under Theodor Benfey. He served as professor at Collège de France and was president of the Société Asiatique (1908–1928), having been vice-president in 1890.

Indologist and linguist Émile-Louis Burnouf studied at ENS, University of Paris, and École française d'Athènes under Jean-Louis and Eugène Burnouf. He held a professorship at University of Nancy (1854–1867) and served as director of École française d'Athènes (1867–1875).

Sinologist and historian Étienne Balázs studied under doctoral supervisor Otto Franke (1923–1930). He later served as a senior researcher at CNRS (1949) and as professor of Chinese economic history at the University of Paris (~1955–1963).

Étienne Lamotte specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at KU Leuven, Rome under Carlo Formichi, and under Louis de La Vallée Poussin. He served as chargé de cours at KU Leuven (1932–1974) and president at UCLouvain (1950–1959).

Working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Ñāṇavīra Thera studied at Magdalene College and under Pelene Siri Vajirañāṇa (~1949–1950). He previously served in the Royal Artillery (1939–1941) and the Intelligence Corps (1941–1945).

Buddhist studies practitioner Ösel Tendzin studied at Fordham University and under Swami Satchidananda Saraswati and Chögyam Trungpa. He was executive vice president at Vajradhatu (1973) and succeeded Trungpa in 1987.

Ülo Valk, a scholar of religious studies and Indology, studied at Miina Härma Gymnasium and the University of Tartu (~1981–1986). He held a post at the University of Tartu (~1995) and edited Numen (~2004–2013).
